# Datasets Used in This Book {#sec-datasets}

Real audit data cannot be published. So every chapter of this book simulates its own data in R. The data is made to look like what auditors receive, and irregularities are *planted* in it for the analysis to find, along with innocent cases that look similar. All names of persons, firms, offices and places are made up, and do not relate to any real entity.

The code that creates the data is shown, folded, at the start of each chapter. Readers can see exactly what was planted, change it, and run it again. The last chapter reads its files from the `Data` folder of the book's repository. The code that creates them is in `tools/make_health_scheme_data.R`, `tools/make_ssy_text_data.R` and `tools/make_ssy_geo_data.R`. The same data is used in several chapters of [*R for Audit Analytics*](https://anilyayavar.github.io/new-book/98-datasets.html).

| Chapter | Data | What is planted |
|----------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| @sec-jet | General ledger of an imaginary State warehousing corporation, 2024-25 with April and May 2025, 16,791 entries in 42,601 lines, with chart of accounts, user master, trial balance and holiday list | A year-end revenue boost entered after closing and reversed; bills booked by a store keeper at night and on holidays; self-approved entries; entries just below an approval limit; round transfers to suspense; a rare account pair; vague narrations; a duplicate entry; a difference with the trial balance |
| @sec-recon | Cash book (2,931 entries) and bank statement (2,916 entries) of an imaginary district health society for 2024-25, with the April 2025 statement; purchase register (641 invoices) and GSTR-2B (600 invoices) of an imaginary company; monthly expenditure by head of a department and the treasury | Unpresented cheques and deposits in transit; bank charges and interest not booked; a transposition error; a cheque never presented; a stale cheque; a self cheque withdrawn but not in the cash book; one credit settling several receipts; cheque numbers written differently or mistyped; credit claimed on invoices suppliers never reported; invoice numbers in different formats; a duplicate claim; a GSTIN failing the check digit; a misclassified bill and an unrecorded salary bill at the treasury |
| @sec-tenderflags | 1,032 works tenders of five departments of an imaginary State, 2022-23 to 2024-25, one row per tender with procedure, publication, dates, evaluation, bids, winner, award, re-tendering and final value | Short bidding windows, quick awards and heavy quality marks in one department, with single bids won by two firms; road works split below the open-tender limit; one firm with a large share of a department's contracts; contracts won low and raised by large variations; calls cancelled until the same firm won |
| @sec-bidrig | Three years of works tenders of a division, with 400 tenders, 1,281 bids, a contractor register and item rates for item-rate tenders | A ring of three firms that takes turns to win; a capable firm that stops bidding in the ring's district; prices that fall when a newcomer enters another district; two bidders sharing a bank account and a director; identical unusual item rates in three tenders |
| @sec-bidshape | 880 larger road and building tenders of a State, 2020-21 to 2024-25, with 5,443 bids and a label for collusive tenders | Two complete cartels whose cover bids are bunched above the winner; an incomplete cartel that faces genuine outsiders |
| @sec-payables | Payables of an imaginary State health directorate with eight district offices, 2024-25. Vendor master (193 vendors) with bank-change log, employee master (320), 1,083 purchase orders, 1,156 goods receipts, 1,089 invoices, 1,073 payments, earlier years' totals, a cement rate contract and monthly bank totals | A bank account changed three days before a large payment and changed back; a vendor registered and paid within a week with no GSTIN; a dormant vendor paid large sums; a duplicate vendor with the same PAN paid the same bill twice; a vendor paid into an employee's account; a GSTIN failing its check; invoices with no order or dated before the order; short deliveries billed in full; rates above the order; payments before receipt; one office paying about 40% more for toner; bills split below a limit; orders at an old contract rate |
| @sec-payroll | Payroll and pensions of an imaginary State water resources department with a head office and eight divisions, 2024-25. Employee master (930) with change log, monthly payroll, arrears bills, sanctioned strength, attendance, pension master (1,572), pension payments, life certificates, commutation payments, bank and treasury totals, and a welfare old age pension list | Pay after resignation and before joining; a pay rise with no order; two increments in a year; arrears paid twice; a bank account changed around an arrears payment; three ghost clerks beyond sanctioned strength with no attendance, sharing a mobile and an account; an employee past superannuation still paid; a 104-year-old pensioner with a 2021 life certificate; service and family pension paid together after a death; commutation paid twice; a pension well above the illustrative rule; two service pensioners on an old age pension list |
| @sec-revenue | Records of an imaginary State tax department on goods and services, 2024-25, with eight districts. Registration master (1,997 dealers), 23,185 monthly returns, movement records and buyers' reports by dealer and month, treasury totals, a rate master with effective dates, 4,897 invoice lines of building material dealers, 112 refunds, 449 demands with collections, and 3,006 property documents with guideline rates | Nil returns while goods move; turnover hidden in round lakh, far below what buyers report; tax falling sharply while the trade grows; tiles taxed at the old rate after a rise; turnovers bunched just under the composition limit and the scheme used in excluded trades; refunds to three new dealers sharing an account and mobile, sanctioned in days; a refund above all tax ever paid; a ring of four shell dealers trading in a circle; dealers who stopped filing or were cancelled but kept trading; property undervalued in one locality, sold twice by one seller, and shops registered as houses; large demands of 2020-21 near the time limit |
| @sec-delays | Applications on the services portal of an imaginary State, 2024-25, cut-off 31 March 2025. 7,785 applications in eight districts and seventeen offices, for caste certificates, pension sanctions, trade licences, water connections and grievances, with dates of receipt and decision, status and the application each reopens | A district that leaves almost half its cases pending, so its closed cases look quick; trade licences recorded as decided on days 28 to 30 just under a 30-day limit; an office that rejects slow cases just before the limit and reopens them under new numbers; an office that transfers slow cases just before the limit; decisions dated before receipt and missing decision dates |
| @sec-ssyaudit | The *Sarvajan Swasthya Yojana* data, an imaginary State health insurance scheme, 2024-25. Hospitals, packages, claims, grievances, patient feedback, a district map, hospital locations, patients' homes and inspections. The files are in the `Data` folder of the book's repository | Six hospitals behaving like camps, with high claims per bed, short stays, weekend admissions, repeated admissions and unbundled packages; two hospitals upcoding to intensive care; grievances and feedback about the camp hospitals; patients travelling far; inspection photos taken away from the hospital |
